thought.text: The `pkill -f` matched my own shell. Let me restart carefully.

reasoning_content:
The pkill killed the shell too perhaps because the command line matched. Let me retry more carefully with a separate command.

Actually exit code 143 = SIGTERM. pkill -f "next-server" may have matched the shell running the command? No. Actually "next dev" string appears in the shell command line itself (the pkill argument), so pkill matched its own parent shell. Let me avoid by using different approach.

action.command: ps aux | grep -i next | grep -v grep | awk '{print $2}' | while read pid; do kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null; done; sleep 3; (ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | grep 3000) || echo "port 3000 free"
